lessons.title: Choosing and Buying Meat
lessons.body: Buying the right meat is the first step to great grilled food. For nyama choma, you want goat or beef. Goat is traditional in East Africa; beef is cheaper and more available. Look for meat from a young animal: goat under 2 years, beef from a 2-3 year old steer. The meat should be bright red, firm, and slightly moist. Avoid dark, dry, or smelly meat. Fat should be white or cream-colored, not yellow. For brochettes, use beef sirloin or rump; for suya, use beef flank or skirt steak. For grilled chicken, buy whole birds or quarters. A whole chicken weighs 1.2-1.8 kg. Buy from a butcher you trust or a market where you can inspect the meat. In Africa, many buy live animals and slaughter on site. If you do, check the animal is healthy: clear eyes, shiny coat, no limping. After slaughter, hang the meat to tenderize for 4-6 hours at cool temperature (below 10Â°C). If you buy from a supermarket, check the expiry date and packaging is intact. Never buy meat that is warm or has been sitting in the sun. For street food, you need consistent supply. Build a relationship with a farmer or butcher. Buy in bulk when prices are low. Refrigerate at 0-4Â°C and use within 2-3 days, or freeze at -18Â°C for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, not on the counter. Good meat is your reputation. Cut costs by buying whole cuts and trimming yourself. But never compromise on freshness.

lessons.title: Marinades and Dry Rubs for African Grilling
lessons.body: Marinades and dry rubs add flavor and tenderize meat. For African grilling, common ingredients include ginger, garlic, chili, lemon, vinegar, oil, and spices like cumin, coriander, paprika, and black pepper. A basic marinade for 1 kg of meat: 4 tablespoons oil, 2 tablespoons lemon juice or vinegar, 1 tablespoon grated ginger, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon chili powder. Mix and rub into meat. Let sit for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge. For suya, use a dry rub: 2 tablespoons ground roasted peanuts, 1 tablespoon paprika, 1 teaspoon cayenne, 1 teaspoon ginger powder, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt. Coat meat before grilling. For nyama choma, many prefer simple salt and pepper, or a wet marinade of oil, garlic, and lemon. Dry rubs are good for chicken and beef. Always pat meat dry before applying dry rub. For marinades, use a non-reactive bowl (glass or plastic). Keep marinade in fridge. Never reuse marinade that touched raw meat unless you boil it. For street food, prepare marinades in bulk and store in squeeze bottles. Label with date. Test flavors: adjust salt and heat to your customers. In West Africa, suya spice is key; in East Africa, nyama choma often uses just salt. You can also add local ingredients: ground crayfish, palm oil, or tamarind. Experiment and find your signature taste. Remember: acidic marinades (lemon, vinegar) can make meat mushy if left too long. Limit to 12 hours for chicken, 24 hours for beef. Sugar in marinade can burn; use low heat. Always grill over medium coals.

lessons.title: Nyama Choma: The Full Method
lessons.body: Nyama Choma is grilled meat, a staple in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. The classic is goat or beef ribs, grilled over charcoal. Start with 2 kg of goat ribs or beef short ribs. Cut into 250-300 g pieces. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Some add lemon juice or pili pili (chili). Let meat come to room temperature for 30 minutes. Prepare charcoal: light 3 kg of lump charcoal in a chimney starter. Wait until coals are covered with grey ash, about 20-30 minutes. Spread coals in a single layer. The fire should be medium-hot: you can hold your hand 15 cm above the grill for 3-4 seconds. Place meat on grill. Sear for 5 minutes per side to lock in juices. Then move to cooler part of grill or raise grill. Cook slowly, turning every 5-7 minutes. Total cooking time: 45-60 minutes for goat ribs, 30-40 minutes for beef. Baste with oil or marinade occasionally. Do not poke meat with a fork; use tongs. Check doneness: internal temperature 70Â°C for medium, 75Â°C for well-done. For authentic nyama choma, cook until well-done but still juicy. Rest meat for 10 minutes before cutting. Serve with kachumbari (tomato, onion, cilantro salad) and ugali. For street food, set up a grill near the road. Display meat on skewers or in a glass case. Price per plate: 200-400 KES depending on cut. Keep coals hot; have a spare chimney. Cook to order for best taste. Hygiene: wear gloves, use clean tongs, cover meat from flies. Nyama choma is social; customers love to see the grilling. Your skill is in timing and seasoning.

lessons.title: Brochettes and Suya Skewers
lessons.body: Brochettes are skewered meat, popular across Africa. Suya is a Nigerian spiced skewer. For brochettes, use 1 kg beef sirloin or lamb, cut into 3 cm cubes. Marinate in oil, garlic, ginger, and soy sauce for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers (soak wooden skewers in water 30 minutes). Leave small gaps between pieces. For suya, use 1 kg beef flank, sliced thin (0.5 cm). Coat with suya spice: 3 tablespoons ground roasted peanuts, 1 tablespoon paprika, 1 teaspoon cayenne, 1 teaspoon ginger, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt. Mix well. Thread onto skewers. Grill over medium-hot charcoal. For brochettes, cook 10-12 minutes, turning every 2 minutes. For suya, cook 5-7 minutes per side, until edges are crisp. Baste with oil to prevent drying. Suya is often served with sliced onions, tomatoes, and extra suya spice. Brochettes can be served with pili pili sauce. For street food, make 50-100 skewers at a time. Keep raw skewers in cooler. Grill to order. Price: 2-3 skewers for 100-200 KES. Use a long grill to cook many at once. Turn with tongs, not hands. For suya, you can also grill over open flame for smoky flavor. Watch for flare-ups; move skewers to cooler side. Test doneness: cut one piece; it should be juicy, not pink. For chicken brochettes, use thigh meat, marinate in yogurt and spices. Always use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables. Clean grill between batches. Serve hot. Suya is best with fresh onion and tomato. You can also add bell peppers and onions to skewers for color. Experiment with spices: some use ground crayfish or stock cubes. Your unique spice mix can become your brand.

lessons.title: Grilled Chicken: Whole and Quarter
lessons.body: Grilled chicken is a best-seller. For whole chicken, buy a 1.5 kg bird. For quarters, buy leg quarters (thigh and drumstick). Marinate for at least 4 hours. Basic marinade: 4 tablespoons oil, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1 tablespoon grated ginger, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. For spicier, add 1 teaspoon chili flakes. Prick chicken with a fork to let marinade in. For whole chicken, truss with string to cook evenly. For quarters, score the skin. Grill over medium heat (coals covered with ash). For whole chicken, cook 60-75 minutes, turning every 15 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75Â°C in the thickest part of the thigh. For quarters, cook 30-40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes. Baste with marinade or oil every 15 minutes. Avoid high heat; chicken burns outside and stays raw inside. Use a meat thermometer. If you don't have one, cut into the thigh; juices should run clear. Rest 10 minutes before serving. For street food, you can grill whole chickens on a rotisserie or on a covered grill. Quarter chickens are easier for portions. Price: whole chicken 500-800 KES, quarter 200-300 KES. Serve with chips (fries), kachumbari, or ugali. For a smoky flavor, add soaked wood chips to coals. Keep raw chicken refrigerated until grilling. Use separate utensils for raw and cooked chicken. Clean surfaces with bleach. For large orders, pre-cook chicken in oven until 90% done, then finish on grill for char. This saves time. Always check doneness. Chicken is safe when internal temperature is 75Â°C. Your customers will return for juicy, well-seasoned chicken.

lessons.title: Sides, Sauces and Accompaniments
lessons.body: Sides and sauces make your grilled meat a full meal. The classic Kenyan side is ugali: white maize meal cooked with water. For 4 people, boil 4 cups water, add 2 cups maize meal, stir until thick. Cook 10 minutes. Serve in slices. Another side is kachumbari: dice 4 tomatoes, 1 red onion, 1 chili, handful cilantro. Mix with lemon juice and salt. For a filling side, serve chips (fries): cut 4 potatoes into sticks, fry at 160Â°C until soft, then at 180Â°C until golden. For sauces, pili pili is essential: blend 10 red chilies, 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tablespoon vinegar, salt. Simmer 10 minutes. For suya, serve extra suya spice and sliced onions. For nyama choma, a simple sauce is lemon and salt. You can also make a peanut sauce: 1 cup ground peanuts, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon tomato paste, chili, salt. Simmer until thick. For brochettes, serve with yogurt mint sauce: 1 cup yogurt, 2 tablespoons chopped mint, 1 garlic clove, salt. For chicken, a barbecue sauce: 1 cup ketchup, 2 tablespoons vinegar, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 teaspoon paprika. Simmer 5 minutes. For street food, prepare sides in bulk. Keep kachumbari fresh; make small batches. Fry chips to order. Have sauces in squeeze bottles. Offer a plate combo: meat, ugali, kachumbari, and sauce. Price: 300-500 KES. For drinks, serve soda, water, or local juice. Hygiene: keep sides covered. Use clean serving spoons. Don't mix raw and cooked. You can also add grilled corn or plantains. Experiment with local ingredients: cassava, matoke, or rice. Your sides should complement the meat, not overpower it. Freshness and presentation matter. A colorful plate sells better. Train your staff to assemble quickly. With good sides, you turn a meat dish into a complete meal.

quiz.q: What color should fresh meat be when buying?
quiz.explanation: Fresh meat is bright red, firm, and slightly moist.

quiz.q: For nyama choma, which animal is traditional in East Africa?
quiz.explanation: Goat is the traditional meat for nyama choma in East Africa.

quiz.q: How long should you hang meat to tenderize after slaughter?
quiz.explanation: Hanging meat for 4-6 hours at cool temperature tenderizes it.

quiz.q: What is the safe refrigerator temperature for storing meat?
quiz.explanation: Meat should be refrigerated at 0-4Â°C to prevent bacterial growth.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common ingredient in African meat marinades?
quiz.explanation: Ginger, garlic, chili, and lemon are common in African marinades.

quiz.q: How long should you marinate chicken in an acidic marinade?
quiz.explanation: Acidic marinades can make chicken mushy if left longer than 12 hours.

quiz.q: What is a key spice in suya?
quiz.explanation: Suya spice is based on ground roasted peanuts, paprika, and cayenne.

quiz.q: Why should you pat meat dry before applying a dry rub?
options: A) To make it stick better
quiz.explanation: Dry meat helps the rub adhere and creates a better crust.

quiz.q: What is the ideal internal temperature for grilled chicken?
quiz.explanation: Chicken is safe to eat when internal temperature reaches 75Â°C.

quiz.q: How long should you rest nyama choma before cutting?
quiz.explanation: Resting for 10 minutes allows juices to redistribute.

quiz.q: What is kachumbari?
options: B) A tomato and onion salad
quiz.explanation: Kachumbari is a fresh salad of tomato, onion, and cilantro.

quiz.q: Which cut is best for brochettes?
quiz.explanation: Beef sirloin or rump is tender and ideal for skewers.

quiz.q: How long should you soak wooden skewers before grilling?
quiz.explanation: Soaking for 30 minutes prevents skewers from burning.

quiz.q: What is the main spice in suya?
quiz.explanation: Suya spice is made from ground roasted peanuts, paprika, and cayenne.

quiz.q: How long do you grill beef brochettes over medium-hot coals?
quiz.explanation: Beef brochettes cook in 10-12 minutes, turning every 2 minutes.

quiz.q: What is a common side for suya?
quiz.explanation: Suya is served with sliced onions, tomatoes, and extra suya spice.

quiz.q: What internal temperature should whole grilled chicken reach?
quiz.explanation: Whole chicken is safe when the thigh reaches 75Â°C.

quiz.q: How long do you grill whole chicken over medium heat?
quiz.explanation: Whole chicken takes 60-75 minutes, turning every 15 minutes.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid high heat when grilling chicken?
options: A) It burns outside and stays raw inside
quiz.explanation: High heat burns the outside before the inside cooks through.

quiz.q: What is a good marinade for grilled chicken?
quiz.explanation: Oil, lemon, garlic, and ginger make a flavorful chicken marinade.

quiz.q: What is ugali made from?
quiz.explanation: Ugali is made from white maize meal cooked with water.

quiz.q: What is pili pili sauce?
quiz.explanation: Pili pili is a spicy sauce made from chilies, tomatoes, and onions.

quiz.q: How do you make chips (fries) crispy?
options: A) Fry once at high heat
quiz.explanation: Double frying gives chips a soft inside and crispy outside.

quiz.q: What is a common accompaniment for nyama choma?
quiz.explanation: Nyama choma is traditionally served with ugali and kachumbari.

quiz.q: Why should you keep raw and cooked meat separate?
quiz.explanation: Separating raw and cooked meat prevents foodborne illness.

quiz.q: What is a good sauce for grilled chicken?
quiz.explanation: Barbecue sauce complements grilled chicken.

quiz.q: How can you add smoky flavor to grilled chicken?
options: A) Add soaked wood chips to coals
quiz.explanation: Soaked wood chips on coals produce smoky flavor.

quiz.q: What is a typical price for a plate of nyama choma in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: A plate of nyama choma typically costs 200-400 KES.

quiz.q: What should you do with leftover marinade that touched raw meat?
quiz.explanation: Marinade that touched raw meat must be boiled before reuse.

quiz.q: What is the best way to check if grilled meat is done?
quiz.explanation: A meat thermometer gives an accurate internal temperature.
